      "Concept Name": "Instruction-fetch program counter",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_frontend",
      "Information": "The current instruction-fetch address selects the next instruction requested from the instruction bus, and the frontend depends on it to follow processor control flow.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The address is exposed on ibus_req_o.addr at line 123, so observing instruction-fetch addresses can disclose execution control flow. The registered address is loaded from ctrl_i.pc_nxt and updated by the bus response at lines 102-114, so tampering can redirect instruction fetches. Fetch progress and subsequent address updates depend on the request state and ibus_rsp_i.ack at lines 101-108 and the request strobe at line 124, so withholding the required response can stall instruction fetching.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could observe or alter the fetch address, or withhold acknowledgements so that the frontend fetches from an unintended location or stops progressing.",

        "ctrl_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [

      "Concept Name": "Fetched instruction stream",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_frontend",
      "Information": "The information is the instruction words fetched from the instruction bus, including compressed words and their decompressed form, which the processor depends on for execution.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "Fetched code can be observed at the frontend_o instruction output after entering from ibus_rsp_i.data at lines 137-138 and being emitted through lines 225, 230, 240, 245 and 268. Changing the response data or the decompressor/input-selection paths at lines 137-138, 190-195 and 219-245 can change the instruction delivered for execution. The instruction is withheld until FIFO availability and acknowledgement-driven reads permit valid output at lines 224, 229, 239, 244, 252-253 and 266-267, so blocking those conditions can stop instruction delivery.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could observe fetched words, inject or alter response data, or prevent the FIFO from becoming available so that execution uses incorrect instructions or stalls.",

        "ibus_rsp_i.data"
      ],

        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"

      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could change ibus_rsp_i.err or the returned fault path so that a failed fetch is reported as valid or a valid fetch is reported as faulty.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "ibus_rsp_i.err"
      ],

      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The mode is loaded from ctrl_i.cpu_priv into fetch.priv at line 115 and copied to ibus_req_o.priv at line 129, so modifying it can cause the bus to authorize or reject a fetch under the wrong privilege context.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could alter the privilege mode carried with a fetch and cause instruction accesses to be performed with an unintended privilege level.",

      "Concept Name": "Instruction-fetch fence command",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_frontend",
      "Information": "The information is the fence qualification carried with an instruction-fetch request, which the instruction bus or memory system uses to apply the requested ordering behavior.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",

        "ctrl_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "ibus_req_o.fence"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        134
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        134
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        134
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C7",
      "Concept Name": "Frontend fetch-stall status",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_frontend",
      "Information": "The information is the status indicating that instruction fetching is halted because the fetch state is requesting data while the prefetch buffer has no free entry; the surrounding processor can depend on it to interpret frontend availability.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The status is produced at frontend_o.halted from fetch.state and ipb.free at line 145, so corrupting the reported status can make the integration logic believe the frontend is available or stalled when it is not.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"

      ],

        145
      ],

      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Fetch and issue sequencing state",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_frontend",
      "Merged Into": "",

    },
